provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism pads the grid by one cell on every side and copies the nearest edge row or column outward. The four new corner cells take the background colour. This operation is symmetric under all eight D4 transforms, because every side gets the same treatment. A rotation or reflection of the input therefore gives the matching rotation or reflection of the output. The emitted program applies the padding directly to the visible grid with no orientation change. The only thing specialised from the factory arguments is the corner colour, which is set to the constant palette[0], the mapped background. Rectangular grids work naturally because the output is always (h+2) x (w+2). Input cells that happen to hold palette[0], such as the 3x3 centre cell, are copied through unchanged.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the corner colour is always the mapped background palette[0], as in the constructor. It does not infer the corner colour from the demonstrations. Grids of size 1 in either dimension also work, because the edge row or column is then the grid itself. No test runs were performed.
